summary: Woodland sits on the dead-flat Sacramento Valley floor just 20 miles northwest of the state capital, and its home-price-to-income ratio of roughly 5.7× puts it in a bracket that's genuinely unusual for a California city this close to a major metro — a median household earning $87,880 faces a $505,200 median home value, which is steep but far less punishing than the Bay Area math that often exceeds 10×. The landscape is wide-open agricultural horizon in every direction, with rice fields and tomato farms pressing right up against city limits; the county is one of California's top agricultural producers, and employers like the Yolo County government, the local school district, and ag-related businesses mean a meaningful share of jobs exist in town rather than requiring a commute down I-5 or Highway 113 to Sacramento. That commute, when it happens, runs roughly 25–35 minutes without traffic but can swell during peak hours on a corridor shared with UC Davis traffic just ten miles south. Summers are searingly hot — average highs well into the 90s with 9.6 hours of daily sunshine — while winters turn cool and tule-fog gray, a rhythm that structures life around early mornings and late evenings from June through September. Downtown's historic grid along Main Street holds a farmers' market, local restaurants, and a compact walkable stretch, but beyond that core the city fragments into standard auto-oriented subdivisions with limited trail connectivity. Median rent at $1,500 keeps the cost of entry relatively accessible, yet property crime runs notably high at over 2,000 per 100K, with motor vehicle theft alone at 438 — a rate that stands out even by Central Valley standards. Woodland is, at its core, an agricultural county seat slowly absorbing Sacramento-region spillover growth, caught between its small-town grid and the subdivision sprawl steadily filling in around it.
